drafted_from: tool:stop-an-email-course's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "End a person's email course subscription from the token in their unsubscribe link, so no further lesson is sent", with {"records":[],"token":"AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA"}. It runs tool:stop-an-email-course and answers {"status":"unsubscribed"}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it keeps nothing and reads no store. Your AI reads the rows it works over from your lists and hands them in (records); the answer holds the rows to keep for your AI to write.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "End a person's email course subscription from the token in their unsubscribe link, so no further lesson is sent", and give it token.
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:stop-an-email-course and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Give token (the unsubscribe token in the link the person was sent). Works out the subscription marked unsubscribed with the time and a stop for that contact over the course's stop scope, and answers them in keep for the caller to write (records: the person's token, subscription and stop rows); an unknown or already used token answers unsubscribed too; a token that is not 32 to 100 letters, digits, - or _ answers malformed and keeps nothing. Answers { status: unsubscribed | malformed }.
4. It keeps nothing and has no records door: it works over the rows you hand in (records) and answers the rows to keep (keep), each with the row it expected, for your AI to write to your store.
